sources.entry: App Uninstaller - Lightweight app uninstaller with drag-and-drop support. Built with Swift and SwiftUI. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/kamjin3086/AppUninstaller) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A lightweight native macOS app uninstaller, built with Swift and SwiftUI, that removes an app and its related support files via drag-and-drop.
summary.what_it_does: You drag a .app file onto the window, and the app scans a set of ~/Library and /Library locations for related files. The scanned locations include Application Support, Preferences (plist), Caches, Logs, Saved Application State, HTTPStorages, WebKit, and Containers. Files are matched by app name (case-insensitive) and bundle identifier. The list of files is shown before deletion and requires confirmation. It requests admin privileges only when needed for system-protected files. The README also mentions a "Deep Cleaning" feature that covers "and more" beyond the listed locations.
use_cases: Completely remove a Mac app along with its leftover files
Clean up preferences, caches and logs after uninstalling an app
Uninstall apps by dragging them onto a window
Find orphaned app data in Library folders
how_to_run: Download AppUninstaller.zip from the Releases page
Unzip and move App Uninstaller.app to /Applications
On first launch, right-click and select Open to bypass Gatekeeper
Build from source: git clone the repo, then run: swift build -c release
Optionally create an app bundle: copy .build/release/AppUninstaller and Info.plist into AppUninstaller.app/Contents
notable: Drag any .app onto the window to start an uninstall
Scans user and system Library locations for leftover files, matched by name and bundle identifier
Shows every file before deletion and asks for confirmation
Requests admin password only when system-protected files need removal
Distributed outside the Mac App Store, since sandboxing would block this access
caveats: Not on the Mac App Store because the App Store sandbox blocks the needed system access
Unsigned release may need right-click Open on first launch to pass Gatekeeper
